title: From one source summary to learned alignment
question: What source information can the decoder use for its next target word?

contribution.text: Use one source summary to condition a phrase score and inspect the reset/update recurrence.

beginner.heading: One source summary, many target predictions
beginner.body: The encoder finishes reading the source before the decoder uses its single summary. Source and target lengths may differ; fixed refers to vector width, not a fixed number of words.

beginner.heading: Score a supplied phrase or generate a new one?
beginner.body: Predict which use the experiment tests, then follow the supplied target prefix and EOS probability. The reported translator adds a neural phrase-pair score to an existing phrase table.

beginner.heading: Ignore before mixing; carry after mixing
beginner.body: Inspect the authored reset and update values. Reset changes the candidate use of prior state; in this paper z weights the old state. The main equation and attachment put reset on different sides of a matrix.

beginner.heading: Name every ingredient in the gain
beginner.body: The baseline test BLEU is 33.30; adding the phrase score gives 33.87. The best 34.64 row also adds a separate language model. An unknown-word penalty is a separate intervention.

beginner.heading: A summary constraint is not a measured length failure
beginner.body: No sentence-length experiment or controlled gate ablation is reported. Selected phrase samples and projected vectors are qualitative inspections.

expert.heading: Reconstruct the conditional score
expert.body: Separate the source summary, target-prefix vocabulary softmax, conditional sequence product and mean log-likelihood. Generation and phrase-table scoring use the same conditional model in different pipelines.

expert.heading: Audit reset placement and z convention
expert.body: Use main Eqs. 5–8 for the archival calculation, and show the attachment alternative separately. The non-diagonal fixture makes reset-before-matrix and reset-after-matrix visibly different; it cannot determine which expression the reported run used.

expert.heading: Bind sampling, dimensions and optimization to their sources
expert.body: Keep unique-pair sampling, shortlist and split roles, main-paper dimensions, conflicting attachment embeddings, initialization and Adadelta settings visible. Missing seeds and runtime details stay missing.

expert.heading: Read the complete four-row canonical table
expert.body: Retain all development/test rows, the separate continuous-space language model, and the aggregate UNK versus particular-word distinction. The earlier preprint table is not substituted.

expert.heading: Separate architecture from causal evidence
expert.body: The ungated observation has no controlled protocol, the samples and t-SNE plots have no quantitative representation test, and this phrase-table experiment does not prove a sentence-length bottleneck.

contribution.text: Initialize a deep recurrent word model from a source summary and compare source order and decoding pipelines.

beginner.heading: Start a word model from the source
beginner.body: A separate encoder summarizes the source; a deep LSTM decoder then predicts target words and an end symbol. The cited Graves formulation is a later gated cell, not the original 1997 cell alone.

beginner.heading: Which pairs get closer after reversal?
beginner.body: Keep original source identities and ordinary target order. Count early and late temporal gaps before comparing their means; the proposed explanation is incomplete and the distances are not measured gradients.

beginner.heading: Generate candidates or rerank a supplied list
beginner.body: Direct beam decoding and phrase-system 1,000-best rescoring have different candidate sources. The 34.81 and 36.5 headlines each use five reversed-source models in those separate pipelines.

beginner.heading: Parallel designs are not an influence arrow
beginner.body: The first manuscript says the system was developed in parallel with Cho. Teaching Cho first does not establish private development order or a causal lineage.

beginner.heading: Successful fixed summaries still have bounded evidence
beginner.body: Length curves describe this test; phrase projections are qualitative. The strongest results include ensembling, vocabulary limits and approximate search.

expert.heading: Factor an EOS-terminated conditional sequence
expert.body: Bind the four-layer encoder/decoder to the named Graves formulation. Likelihood on observed prefixes, generation on model prefixes and approximate search are different operations.

expert.heading: Keep parameter counts version-bound
expert.body: Read the selected corpus, vocabularies, training and parallelism conditions. Proceedings and v1–v2 report 380 million parameters; v3 reports 384 million and adds a state characterization.

expert.heading: Count gaps without turning them into gradients
expert.body: Under the fixture EOS convention derive forward and reversed gaps per original source identity. Keep the unchanged mean and changing early/late gaps together, with the prose/table score discrepancy.

expert.heading: Audit both complete result pipelines
expert.body: Retain beam sizes, number of models, source order, candidate-system identity, score averaging and oracle scope in both tables. Do not difference scores from unmatched pipeline conditions.

expert.heading: Read the parallel-development statement in v1
expert.body: The canonical proceedings citation omits the explicit parallel wording. The editorial Cho comparison permits no causal claim.

expert.heading: Audit length, projections and missing controls
expert.body: The length plot lacks a matched unreversed curve and numeric bins; PCA lacks a systematic representation test. No matched full component ablation or uncertainty estimate is supplied.

contribution.text: Compute a decoder-conditioned weighted source read at each target step.

beginner.heading: Replace one shared summary with a new source read
beginner.body: The fixed-vector bottleneck is a conjecture. This extension computes a weighted context at each step; each context still has fixed width.

beginner.heading: What stays fixed when the target step changes?
beginner.body: Hold the supplied bidirectional annotation bank fixed and change the authored prior decoder state. Trace energies, source weights and coordinate contributions. Equal scores and identical annotations test when a new step need not change the read.

beginner.heading: A source weight is not a target-word probability
beginner.body: Source softmax distributes weight over source positions; a separate vocabulary softmax predicts a target word. Joint training uses translation loss, not supplied gold word alignments. The fixture does not train or translate.

beginner.heading: Compare named test conditions
beginner.body: Keep All and No UNK columns and the longer-trained starred run separate. Attention, bidirectionality and capacity change together; length trends cannot isolate compression as the cause.

beginner.heading: Reordering differs from a forward-moving handwriting window
beginner.body: Graves is a named comparison, not a causal derivation. Early manuscripts also cite each other across the Sutskever and Bahdanau branches; public posting dates cannot establish private development order.

expert.heading: Reconstruct energy, source denominator and context
expert.body: Use the accepted v5 additive scorer with supplied states and concatenated forward/backward annotations. Show projected terms, tanh activations, stable exponentials, source normalizer and signed context contributions.

expert.heading: Keep stable main-text order and conflicting appendices separate
expert.body: Prior state precedes the read, then the updated state precedes output. Preserve the v5/v6/v7 decoder-index and matrix conflicts and the opposite Cho z convention; no hybrid gate-level decoder is evaluated.

expert.heading: Audit capacity, shortlist and training time
expert.body: Retain the selected data, split roles, encoder direction counts, hidden dimensions, training caps, all five training durations and approximate beam search.

expert.heading: Read both BLEU conditions without causal compression claims
expert.body: Keep all six All/No UNK rows and the longer-trained run. Length plots are descriptive and capacity changes with the mechanism; rare words remain unresolved.

expert.heading: Audit comparison and reciprocal manuscript awareness
expert.body: Inspect the version-specific Graves and Sutskever passages. A monotonic unnormalized handwriting window differs from source-softmax translation reads; neither chronology nor comparison establishes a causal edge.

expert.heading: A heatmap does not validate an alignment posterior
expert.body: The paper supplies qualitative attention matrices without a quantitative alignment benchmark or matched component-only ablations. The synthetic read demonstrates arithmetic only.

contribution.text: Compare current-state attention, source support and attentional input feeding.

beginner.heading: Read all positions or a neighborhood
beginner.body: The stacked-LSTM decoder scores from its current state. Global attention reads every source state; local attention restricts support. Static support diagrams show what a window can omit without inventing unresolved numerical weights.

beginner.heading: Where does the previous attentional summary go?
beginner.body: Trace the previous attentional vector into the next target input. It supplies history but does not certify which words have been translated.

beginner.heading: Name the inherited recipe and the attention extension
beginner.body: Luong cites the stacked-LSTM/reversal recipe and Bahdanau-style soft alignment separately; their qualified relations carry different mechanisms.

beginner.heading: A result ladder changes several ingredients
beginner.body: The 14.0 to 19.0 path changes attention, score, locality and input feeding. Unknown replacement and eight-model ensembling are separate additions.

beginner.heading: Translation quality and extracted alignment are different tests
beginner.body: The alignment protocol has different data and link-extraction conditions. Lower alignment error need not mean better translation or a more faithful explanation.

expert.heading: Score from the current decoder state
expert.body: Reconstruct the current-state global path and previous-attentional-vector input feeding. Keep its LSTM/reversal recipe distinct from the Bahdanau extension.

expert.heading: Audit score shapes, windows and later corrections
expert.body: Keep location, unscaled dot, general and v5-corrected concat separate. Local-m and local-p remain static source operations; Gaussian multiplication does not license an implicit final normalization.

expert.heading: Bind metrics and hyperparameters to the version
expert.body: Retain language direction, filtering, vocabulary, training regime and tokenized versus NIST BLEU. Dropout p and D occur only in the later revision.

expert.heading: Read all component and architecture tables
expert.body: Keep English–German and German–English ladders, WMT15 ensemble, unknown replacement, incomplete score/scope sweep and failed/no-BLEU cells separate.

expert.heading: Audit descriptive length and alignment evidence
expert.body: Length plots lack numeric bins and matched controls. AER uses forced reference decoding and selected links under unmatched training conditions; incomplete factorial controls limit causal rankings.

interludes.title: From word probability to a source-conditioned sequence

beginner.heading: Add the source to the prediction question
beginner.body: Return to recurrent next-word softmax, then supply a source–target pair and a possibly different-length EOS-terminated target. The next distribution depends on source summary and target prefix.

expert.heading: Separate normalization, likelihood and search
expert.body: Vocabulary normalization occurs at each prefix. Conditional sequence likelihood multiplies observed-target factors including EOS; generation uses its own prefixes and search is approximate. The authored output fixture evaluates no recurrent decoder.

beginner.heading: Keep the later cell separate from the original
beginner.body: The cited formulation has input, forget and output gates and state-to-gate connections. This source bridge introduces no handwriting window into the translator.

expert.heading: Read the formulation and training boundary
expert.body: Graves v5 Eqs. 7–11 read previous cell state for input/forget gates and updated state for output, with diagonal state-to-gate weights and full BPTT. Citation does not establish every implementation detail of the target.

interludes.title: A monotonic handwriting window is a comparison

beginner.heading: A forward-moving window cannot arbitrarily reorder
beginner.body: Positive location increments move handwriting windows forward. Their unnormalized character weights differ from translation source-softmax weights, and the named comparison permits no causal derivation.

expert.heading: Preserve window normalization and version scope
expert.body: Read Graves v5 window mechanism and earlier formula corrections separately. The translation paper compares the monotonicity limit; this bridge calculates neither handwriting output nor a local-p translation window.
